reasons.D: Keeps the passage's deadpan mock-endorsement ('mere churlishness', 'proper public spirit', 'that was well too') with the same mix of short plain sentences and cumulative ones, period diction, and a dry epigrammatic close without overdoing it.
reasons.C: Strong period register and ironic reasonableness close to the author, but slightly more polished and aphoristic ('bulge in unexpected places'), leaning a touch toward knowing wit over the passage's straight-faced irony.
reasons.B: Period feel and semicolon use fit, but the stance turns openly sympathetic and confessional at the end, dropping the sustained irony that carries the passage.
reasons.A: Modern, plain, short-sentence rhythm and a sincere reportorial stance; little of the passage's ironic mock-argument or period diction.
